• New agreements with Kinsus and Samsung Electro-Mechanics support additional substrate capacity and expanded production capabilities at existing factories.

• NVIDIA’s work with Amkor and SPIL expands advanced packaging capacity for current and next-generation accelerated computing platforms.

• NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 and Vera CPUs began volume shipments in the third quarter, leveraging TSMC’s 5nm, 3nm and CoWoS advanced packaging technologies.

• Foxconn is deepening its collaboration with NVIDIA, drawing on its global production network to support next-generation GPU and networking platforms.

NVIDIA today announced expanded commitments with supply chain partners to support sustainable long-term growth, aligning supply and manufacturing capacity with demand for its accelerated computing and AI infrastructure platforms.

Working with Amkor Technology, Foxconn, Kinsus Interconnect Technology, Samsung Electro-Mechanics , Siliconware Precision Industries (SPIL) and TSMC, NVIDIA is expanding manufacturing capacity across substrates, advanced packaging, wafer and contract manufacturing to scale production of its current and next-generation accelerated computing platforms.

“Our supply chain is a strategic advantage,” said Debora Shoquist, executive vice president of operations at NVIDIA. “Our work with these partners builds on our manufacturing foundation for long-term growth, expanding capacity across components, advanced packaging and system production to deliver the accelerated computing platforms our customers need.”

Increasing Substrate Capacity and Production Capabilities NVIDIA is expanding its substrate supply commitments with Kinsus and Samsung Electro-Mechanics, adding manufacturing capacity and improving production capabilities at existing factories.

Under a new agreement with NVIDIA, Kinsus plans to expand its advanced ABF package substrate manufacturing capacity dedicated to NVIDIA by more than 3.5x over current levels from its Youth campus in Taoyuan, Taiwan.

Production is expected to begin in the second half of 2027, with the additional capacity targeted for the third quarter of 2028. This multiyear agreement builds on the companies’ existing supplier relationship and supports NVIDIA’s long-term supply planning for its accelerated computing platforms.

“We believe AI will be one of the most important technology transitions of our lifetime,” said Scott Chen, CEO and president of Kinsus. “After more than a decade of partnership with NVIDIA, we are excited to continue building the future together.”

NVIDIA and Samsung Electro-Mechanics have amended their existing substrate supply agreement to improve operational capabilities at existing factories in support of increased production of NVIDIA’s accelerated computing platforms.

The amendment builds on the companies’ previously announced multiyear collaboration supporting substrate manufacturing in Sejong and Busan, South Korea, for NVIDIA’s compute and high-speed networking technologies.

“By combining our world-class substrate fine-processing technology and high-reliability MLCC technology, we will perfectly fulfill our role as a total solution provider so that NVIDIA’s AI platform can be supplied to the global market on time, with the highest performance and quality,” said Duck-Hyun Chang, CEO of Samsung Electro-Mechanics.

Scaling Advanced Packaging Through Multiyear Agreements NVIDIA’s advanced packaging plans include a new capacity expansion with SPIL and previously announced agreements supporting Amkor’s manufacturing expansion in the U.S. and South Korea.

NVIDIA is supporting Amkor’s expansion of advanced packaging capacity in Arizona and South Korea through multiyear agreements announced in July and October 2026, totaling nearly $3 billion. The agreements include prepayments to help Amkor scale manufacturing capacity for NVIDIA’s long-term production needs.

“Our agreements with NVIDIA support investments in Arizona and South Korea that will serve multiple generations of AI platforms,” said Kevin Engel, president and CEO of Amkor. “That long-term planning allows us to advance our packaging technologies and add manufacturing capacity as NVIDIA’s production needs grow.”

NVIDIA and SPIL are expanding advanced packaging operations in Taiwan under a multiyear agreement supported by multibillion-dollar funding from NVIDIA. The expansion will increase contracted advanced packaging capacity dedicated to NVIDIA by mid-2029.

The project includes new production lines with turnkey support spanning bumping, interposer wafer fabrication, assembly and testing. These capabilities support semiconductor products with demanding requirements for computing performance, bandwidth, power efficiency and system integration.

“SPIL is proud to strengthen our collaboration with NVIDIA,” said C.W. Tsai, CEO and chairman of the board of SPIL. “This agreement enhances our ability to support next‑generation packaging technologies and deliver the performance and reliability required for future AI systems.”

Next-Generation Technologies for Agentic AI The third quarter marked the first volume shipment of NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 and Vera CPUs for agentic AI. These products take advantage of TSMC’s 5nm, 3nm and CoWoS advanced packaging technologies.

“TSMC and NVIDIA share a longstanding partnership built on semiconductor innovation,” said Dr. Kevin Zhang, senior vice president and deputy co-COO at TSMC. “This deep collaboration allows us to plan for future technology requirements and prepare our manufacturing capabilities as NVIDIA brings new platforms to market.”

أعلنت NVIDIA عن توسيع التزاماتها مع شركاء سلسلة التوريد، بهدف مواءمة الطاقة الإنتاجية مع الطلب المتزايد على منصات الحوسبة المتسارعة والبنية التحتية للذكاء الاصطناعي.

• اتفاقيات جديدة مع Kinsus وSamsung Electro-Mechanics لزيادة سعة ركائز التغليف وتحسين القدرات الإنتاجية في المصانع القائمة.

• ستوسّع Kinsus طاقتها المخصصة لـ NVIDIA في ركائز ABF بأكثر من 3.5 أضعاف المستوى الحالي في تايوان، على أن يبدأ الإنتاج في النصف الثاني من 2027 وتُستكمل الطاقة الإضافية في الربع الثالث من 2028.

• التعاون مع Amkor وSPIL يوسّع سعة التغليف المتقدم للمنصات الحالية والقادمة.

• بدأت شحنات Vera Rubin NVL72 ومعالجات Vera بكميات كبيرة في الربع الثالث، باستخدام تقنيات TSMC بدقة 5 و3 نانومتر وCoWoS.

• تعمّق Foxconn تعاونها مع NVIDIA لدعم وحدات المعالجة والشبكات من الجيل القادم.

وقالت ديبورا شوكويست، نائبة الرئيس التنفيذي للعمليات، إن سلسلة التوريد ميزة استراتيجية للشركة.

تكمن أهمية الخبر في أن توافر الركائز والتغليف المتقدم يمثل عنق زجاجة رئيسياً في إنتاج شرائح الذكاء الاصطناعي.
